status: pre-registered. Commit this file before any scored run. The harness refuses to run if the file is not committed.
question: Does plain Claude Code still lose on large aggregation tasks, so that an llm_map tool is worth building?
score_metric: mean OOLONG score (scorer.py), cleaned set, best plain arm = the higher mean of A and B at the decision length

map_plan_estimate_usd_per_task.basis: scratchpad lcm-gap-review.md section 5.4: all items go once through a small model, about 150 prompt tokens per item, plus about $0.30 of main-model control. The value is a proposal. The user confirms it before the first scored slice run.
map_plan_estimate_usd_per_task.registered_by: pre-registered by the orchestrator 2026-11-18; may be changed by Pratik only before the full eval, never after seeing the full-eval data

build_llm_map_if: best plain arm mean score at 128K is 0.70 or less
OR best plain arm cost per task at 128K is more than 2.0 times map_plan_estimate_usd_per_task
rule.do_not_build_if: best plain arm mean score at 128K is 0.85 or more AND its cost per task is within 1.5 times map_plan_estimate_usd_per_task
rule.otherwise: the user decides, with the table

sample_size_note: 30 paired tasks per arm see only a gap of 0.15 or more. With a paired SD of about 0.3 the 95 percent half-width is about 0.11. A smaller gap is not a result. The report prints this note.
not_a_decision: A run with fewer than 10 paired tasks at the decision length (for example the 2-task pilot) never applies this rule. The report prints 'rule not applied'.
